taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Tridens buckleyanus normalized to current accepted Tridentopsis buckleyana.
look_here_first: BUCKLEY TRIDENTOPSIS (Buckley tridens): look for an OPEN, broadly ovate panicle whose straight primary branches spread or ascend well away from the axis, with small separated spikelets. The original card's 'compact/fluffy' shortcut is inconsistent with the existing photo and Kew GrassBase. Verify 3–5 fertile florets, usually 7–10 mm spikelets and dorsal lemma hairs on an intact mature specimen; county-native certification stays provisional.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local source; WFO 2026 accepts Tridentopsis buckleyana and lists Tridens buckleyanus as a synonym.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; exact target-zone county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Poaceae: use growth habit, ligule, panicle architecture, spikelet form, lemma hairs and awns. For this old Tridens complex, panicle openness/color and current genus placement are especially useful.
best_field_traits: Warm-season perennial of Central Texas with openly separated branches and scattered multi-flowered spikelets, not a fluffy compact spike. Kew's synonym treatment of Tridens buckleyanus gives an open ovate 10–28 cm panicle, long distant branches, 7–10 mm spikelets and 3–5 fertile florets. These measurements and hairs are SOURCE traits, not verified in today's photograph.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Compared with T. mutica, the best gross clue is a spreading, open panicle rather than a slender column of closely ascending branches. Buckleyana tends 3–5 florets/spikelet versus 5–11 in mutica, but 5 overlaps; lengths overlap at 8–10 mm. Verify by dissection, not head shape alone. Historical Tridens buckleyanus is a synonym, not another species card.
crew_field_check: FIRST: original grass photograph visibly shows an open flowering head with separated primary branches; do NOT teach the former compact/fluffy shortcut.
Photograph the WHOLE intact panicle with ruler (Kew: generally 10–28 cm), noting primary branch angles and distances.
Under 10–20×, COUNT fertile florets on 3 mature spikelets (usually 3–5), and MEASURE spikelets (often 7–10 mm).
Separate the outer glumes and one lemma: check its three nerves, their basal hairs and the lemma length (source ~4–6 mm), not resolved in source image.
Show short ciliate membranous ligule and blade/sheath collar for grass morphology; shared with mutica and not a shortcut.
If only a cut loose branch is present or overlapping five-floret spikelets, leave Tridentopsis sp. or provisional source ID.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Complete mature open ovate panicle and basal culm against centimeter scale
Long distantly attached panicle branches alongside the narrow mutica head, matched view
Three ripe whole spikelets with millimeter scale and each fertile floret numbered
Detached 3-veined fertile lemma dorsal face under 10–20× showing basal midvein and margin hairs
True ciliate membranous ligule and rooted bunchgrass habit with local voucher

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Open, broadly ovate 10–28 cm panicle with long, widely separated 4–13 cm branches; confirm three to five fertile florets on each of several measured mature spikelets. Panicle openness is a first clue, not a complete species determination.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form_collar: Tufted perennial; culms approximately 40–80 cm; blades about 1–4 mm wide. True ligule is a ciliate membrane approximately 0.4–1 mm, with glabrous collar in GrassBase; show actual blade–sheath junction, not nearby node hairs.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet_glumes: Spikelets approximately 7–10 mm long, 2–3 mm wide, usually 3–5 fertile florets. Persistent lower glume approximately 5–6 mm, usually slightly LONGER than upper glume (approximately 4–5 mm); both one-veined in GrassBase. Count florets on three intact spikelets.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lemma_palea_awn: Fertile lemmas approximately 4–6 mm, three-veined; midvein and lower margins hairy. Palea approximately 3–5 mm. Lemma tips awnless or shortly mucronate, NOT long-awned. Show actual dorsal nerve hairs in a dissected floret.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Tridentopsis mutica has a very narrow contracted panicle (~0.3–0.8 cm wide) and typically 5–11 fertile florets. Five florets and 8–10 mm spikelets overlap; compare entire head plus glumes and dorsal lemma hairs. Tridens texanus and airy Eragrostis also require multifloret/lemma inspection.
precise_photo_arrow_gaps: Same rooted Texas plant: complete ovate panicle, 1-cm ruler and widely separated branch insertion points.
Three attached mature spikelets with 1-mm scale, numbered fertile florets and both persistent glumes; confirm lower glume > upper.
Detached 4–6 mm three-veined lemma, dorsal face at 20× showing actual basal midvein/margin hairs; no arrow unless pixels resolve them.
True ciliate membranous ligule at blade–sheath joint with 1-mm bar and matched mutica panicle at equal scale.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Preserve original CC BY-NC photo, taxonomy/target-zone holds and existing three gross arrows. Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until local taxon-vetted scaled spikelet and lemma hair evidence, per-image rights, pixel-accurate arrows and public learner QA are confirmed.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.source_scope: Published GrassBase morphology under historical synonym Tridens buckleyanus; not measurements from existing image; no county nativity conclusion.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Tridentopsis: first branches, then florets
steps: 1 · Ground-level bunch: use gallery panel 1 (Sam Kieschnick), whose actual pixels show a green/dry leaf tuft anchored in soil. Soil conceals actual root crown and short rhizome; do not point at a presumed underground organ. New panels 9–10 show close hand-held basal sheaths and basal fibers from the same Bandera source observation, but no rooted crown/rhizome with a scale.

2 · Flowering structure: gallery panels 2–3 and 7 show wide separated OPEN Buckley panicle branches. Do NOT use the old 'compact/fluffy' cue; whole mature panicle and branch insertion are first field clues.

3 · Node versus ligule: gallery panel 4 is a real green leaf joining a culm by a stem node; the free inner ciliate membranous ligule is NOT photographed. In the field peel and open an actual attached leaf sheath and use a 1-mm ruler. See panels 11–12 for exact-species blade/sheath transitions, including Woodcreek in Hays County; do not claim a fully exposed ligule.
4 · Reproductive units: panels 5–8 show actual mature multifloret spikelets and flowering branches. Glume/lemma boundaries and pubescence must not be invented from edge fuzz.

5 · Look-alike: panels 13–15 are DIFFERENT SPECIES Tridentopsis mutica, with narrow contracted heads. The two species can overlap in lengths and five-floret spikelets; do not certify Buckley from one head alone.

6 · Field evidence needed: single same-vouchered rooted flowering clump, exposed basal rhizome/root origin, inner ciliate membrane, and (only if cryptic overlap remains) ripe 3–5-floret spikelets and hairy three-veined lemma photographed beside mm scale.

7 · Respect rights: preserve exact jamiemandell CC BY-NC image with source attribution and noncommercial-only condition, seven CC BY 4.0 originals plus four new image-level CC BY-NC originals, and existing Joey CC BY-NC different-species comparisons. Source/botanical determination remains provisional where not voucher-confirmed.

2026-10-27 photograph closeout: source-reviewed eight new candidate originals (Eric Knight, Andy Blair and others) but none actually shows a free 0.4–1 mm ciliate ligule with a real scale. Do not borrow the misidentified Wilman lovegrass image; move on to other grass species for crew-level learning, retain strict FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until photographed on same-vouchered specimen.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Do not finalize at species if whole-panicle context is absent or floret count sits in overlapping range; dissect true ripe spikelet with scale.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Fifteen comparison gallery panels = twelve archived same-species photos including conditional CC BY-NC + three DIFFERENT-SPECIES slim Tridentopsis photos. Original panel 4 is culm/node, newer panels 11–12 show blade/sheath transitions but not a measured free 0.4–1 mm ligule. New hand-held basal photos show tight live/dry tillers and short basal strands, NOT exposed same-vouchered roots/rhizome plus cm scale. FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST — OPEN, NOT COMPACT
field_id_short_tiles.short: Broadly ovate 10–28 cm panicle with widely spaced, spreading or ascending 4–13 cm branches.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Actual field photo (gallery panel 1) shows a tightly converging living bunch near soil level, but exposed root fibers and the buried basal rhizome are not pictured. Gallery panels 2–3 show OPEN widely branching flowering heads (not a compact fluffy head); panel 7 reinforces how widely separated flowering branches carry spikelets. Published GrassBase under synonym Tridens buckleyanus describes a broad 10–28 cm mature panicle and 4–13 cm lateral branches, not measurements independently made from these photos. Gallery panels 9–10 add a physically collected Bandera compact leafy base and exposed dry sheaths; short rootlike strands are not a cleaned measured root network.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SPECIES HABIT PANELS — SAME-PLANT PANICLE SCALE STILL NEEDED

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · TRUE LIGULE AND COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: A 0.4–1 mm ciliate membranous ligule is a PUBLISHED trait, not photographically measured here.
field_id_short_tiles.details: The exact source-licensed Eric Knight photograph (gallery panel 4) shows a green leaf joining the culm near its node. On the inspected pixels this is a visible leaf attachment/culm NODE region, NOT an opened sheath with a clearly resolved free ciliate ligule; the earlier generic blade–sheath terminology overstated the image. A true species-specific 0.4–1 mm ciliate membrane requires gently peeling open the inner sheath of a verified flowering plant and focusing beside a 1-mm ruler. Gallery panel 11 is a Bandera blade/sheath transition, panel 12 is a separate Hays County local collar region. Neither actually isolates or measures the short true inner ciliate ligule.
field_id_short_tiles.status: LEAF ATTACHMENT/TRUE CULM NODE VISIBLE — INNER LIGULE STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · COUNT FLORETS; SEPARATE BOTH GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Spikelets 7–10 mm with usually 3–5 fertile florets; lower glume 5–6 mm, upper 4–5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Gallery panels 5–8 show real source-determined Buckley spikelets: attached mature units, a detached spikelet, attached flowering units and an enlarged whole mature unit. They do NOT establish measured individual glumes or floret count, and should not include the panel 4 leaf/node picture. Published GrassBase measurements under historical Tridens buckleyanus describe 7–10 mm spikelets, 3–5 fertile florets, lower persistent glume commonly 5–6 mm and upper 4–5 mm; verify in several ripe spikelets with a 1-mm scale only when distinguishing the overlapping slim Tridentopsis.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL SPIKELET PHOTOS — NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO DISSECTION WITH 1-MM SCALE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · THREE-VEINED LEMMA; NO LONG AWN
field_id_short_tiles.short: Fertile lemma 4–6 mm, three-veined, hairy low on midvein and margins; palea 3–5 mm.
field_id_short_tiles.details: GrassBase describes a blunt or notched lemma apex, awnless or only minutely mucronate. Isolate one mature floret to show the lemma's dorsal face, its basal hairs, and the palea. The available overview/spikelet images cannot verify submillimeter hairs or the exact lemma tip. No microscopic arrows are justified until pixels resolve those structures.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · LOCAL LOOK-ALIKES — SLIM TRIDENTOPSIS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Buckley: open spreading head, often 3–5 florets; slim: 0.3–0.8 cm-wide contracted head, often 5–11.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Panels 13–15 show Tridentopsis mutica, NOT Buckley. Five florets and 8–10 mm spikelets overlap, so these measurements alone do not confirm species. Compare complete same-scale panicles, branch angles, glume proportions, and verified lemma hair distribution. Tridens texanus and airy Eragrostis can also mislead; color is not a reliable separator.
field_id_short_tiles.status: REAL OTHER-SPECIES COMPARISON — OVERLAP REQUIRES MATURE DISSECTION

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · PUBLIC-READY GATE / TWO HANDOFFS
field_id_short_tiles.short: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS: 12 archived Buckley JPEGs, 15 panels total; true measured ligule and connected rooted crown still missing.
field_id_short_tiles.details: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: one connected rooted live perennial with exposed knotty crown/short rhizome and full open 10–28 cm panicle; opened true inner 0.4–1 mm ciliate membranous ligule beside 1-mm scale; three ripe 7–10 mm spikelets with measured glumes, floret counts and three-veined hairy lemma only when slim tridens overlap persists. NEEDS_SITE_QA: 12 existing exact-species JPEGs (seven CC BY and five CC BY-NC) plus three explicitly OTHER-SPECIES slim tridens comparison panels, all 15 panel indices, actual visible arrow endpoints and rights-filtered mobile display. Aboveground sheaths and a Hays County collar-region photograph do NOT establish a measured free ligule or exposed connected rhizome. Preserve provisional taxonomy/native-range holds.

grass_species_finalization_20261027.scope: Existing canonical Tridentopsis buckleyana species identification only; no new images, annotations, taxonomy/range, genus/family, website or Pages changes.

existing_evidence.photographed: Open spreading flowering panicles, attached multifloret spikelets, living basal tufts, hand-held lower sheaths and a Hays County blade/sheath transition.
existing_evidence.not_photographed: Excavated connected rooted crown/rhizome, isolated free inner ciliate ligule with calibrated length, measured paired glumes or dorsal lemma nerve hairs.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: One taxon-authenticated living rooted bunch photographed continuously from its open 10–28 cm ovate panicle with 4–13 cm spreading branches to exposed attached root crown; show actual knotty short rhizome if present and centimeter ruler.

Open an attached inner blade–sheath junction and isolate the published 0.4–1 mm ciliate membranous ligule against a 1-mm scale; existing Hays and Bandera junction images show external transition, not free measured ligule.
If slim tridens remains confusable, dissect three ripe 7–10 mm Buckley spikelets and count the usually 3–5 fertile florets; separately measure lower glume ~5–6 mm and upper ~4–5 mm under 1-mm scale.

If five-floret/8–10 mm overlap persists, isolate a 4–6 mm three-veined awnless/minutely mucronate fertile lemma and palea, photographing real basal midvein/marginal hairs under magnification; do not annotate unresolved hair pixels.
Matched verified Buckley OPEN versus slim tridens NARROW contracted whole panicles photographed at equal scale and comparable maturity; do not substitute color or a single five-floret spikelet.
